title: Human Blood Types
text: Human blood type is determined by the presence or absence of certain antigens on the surface of red blood cells. The ABO blood group system, discovered by Karl Landsteiner in 1901, classifies blood into four types: A, B, AB, and O. The Rh blood group system, based on the presence or absence of the RhD antigen, further divides blood into positive or negative. In blood transfusions, compatibility between donor and recipient is critical; incompatible transfusions can cause life-threatening immune reactions. Type O negative blood is considered the universal donor, while type AB positive is the universal recipient. Knowledge of blood types is also important in organ transplantation and prenatal care.
